chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the adhān from the minaret: is it a sunnah (prophetic tradition)? He said: “The adhān used only to be called for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم on the ground, and at that time there was no minaret.”

key_terms.أَسُنَّةٌ: whether it is an established sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.الْمَنَارَةِ: the minaret from which the call may be given
key_terms.فِي الْأَرْضِ: on the ground level, not from an elevated structure
key_terms.مَنَارَةٌ: a minaret; a tower structure for the call

ai.seo_question: Is calling the adhān from a minaret part of the sunnah (prophetic tradition)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses whether giving the adhān from a minaret is part of the sunnah (prophetic tradition). The Imam عليه السلام explains that during the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the adhān was given on the ground and there was no minaret, indicating that the use of a minaret is not itself an established sunnah.
